correctness.rationale: Each matching face uniquely splits into an original-edge matching M and pendant edges T at uncovered original vertices. Toggle the leaf at the least uncovered vertex as a face-poset matching, with exactly the perfect matchings of G left unmatched. Directed Hasse edges may only decrease the original-edge matching M except for pendant additions at a fixed pivot. Within each M fiber no unmatched arrow re-adds any deleted nonpivot leaf and the pivot cannot be removed after its matched upward insertion; hence global acyclicity. Reduced Forman Morse gives precisely p(G) cells in dimension k-1 plus a basepoint; the n=2 zero-dimensional edge case yields S^0 and odd n cannot have perfect matching. Source VERIFY.py inspected for correct independent Hasse acyclicity and mod-two checks, which are finite corroboration only.

This is the full claimed result; no new equivariant, persistence or signed-basis theorem is added.
